headline: Election Day opens with Monday's oil trade partly reversing: a WSJ-reported U.S. strike on Iran's Qeshm Island has Brent back ≈$105–107 after Monday's 7.6% crash, gold is ≈$3,900 (−1%) and Apple's margin warning has S&P futures slightly lower. Monday's oil-driven bull-flattener (10Y ≈4.9%) now has to get through JOLTS (9 AM CT), tonight's midterms and Wednesday's 7:30 AM refunding with a December hike still ≈75% priced.
summary: Oil gave back part of Monday's crash overnight. Brent fell 7.6% Monday to ≈$104–105 on Iran–Qatar talk hopes, then bounced ≈1–2% to ≈$105–107 (WTI ≈$97–98) after the WSJ reported a limited, 'defensive' U.S. strike on Qeshm Island near Hormuz. An Iranian official told Reuters the sides remain 'far from' a deal. Oil is the swing factor for both breakevens and December hike odds, so watch whether Monday's 4–5 bp long-end rally holds.

Rates enter the day bull-flattened. Monday closes: 10Y ≈4.89–4.91%, 30Y ≈5.26–5.29% (lowest since September), 2Y ≈4.56–4.60% (sources differ by snapshot). 2s10s ≈31–32 bp. FedWatch has a Dec 8–9 hike at ≈72–77%, down from ≈85% right after the Oct 28 10–2 hold. The front end won't move much before Friday's payrolls (≈55k).

Equities: S&P futures ≈−0.05% to −0.2%, Dow futures ≈−0.5%, Nasdaq-100 futures ≈+0.1% to +0.4% (≈5:40 AM ET snapshots). Apple fell ≈4.5% pre-market after guiding December-quarter gross margin to 45–46% (from 47.9%) on 'unprecedented' memory costs, despite record $114.5B revenue (+12%). Palantir beat ($2.31B revenue, +96%; FY guide raised to ≈$8.53B) and still fell ≈4–8%. AMD reports after the close (≈$1.95 EPS on ≈$13.1B; options imply ≈±11%).

Global front end stays hawkish. The RBA hiked 25 bp to 4.85% overnight in a 6–3 vote, its fifth hike of 2026 and the highest cash rate since 2008, but it dropped its tightening-bias language. Several desks now call this the peak. The BoE and Norges Bank decide Thursday. The 10Y gilt is ≈5.20–5.24% and the Bund ≈3.30% (lowest since late August).

Metals are back under pressure. Spot gold is ≈$3,900 (−1.1%) after failing near $3,970. Silver is ≈$49.8–50.2, and platinum (−2.1%) and palladium (−2.9%) are also down. The World Gold Council halved its 2026 investment-demand growth forecast to 200t as Q3 bar/coin demand fell 19%, even as central-bank buying jumped 42% to 321t. LME copper rose 1.4% Monday to ≈$14,349/t on Chile supply cuts, despite LME stocks at a 3½-month high.

Capital markets: Anthropic's amended S-1 shows ≈$17B Q3 revenue (≈+1,127% y/y) and a $23.3B net loss, mostly non-cash. Investor valuation talk has slipped to ≈$1.5T from ≈$2T, with Goldman and Morgan Stanley leading 22 banks. Tonight's midterm result (FXStreet cites ≈71% odds of a Democratic Senate) is the overnight fiscal and term-premium catalyst before Treasury's refunding statement at 7:30 AM CT Wednesday.

calendar.event: Earnings: Pfizer, Shopify, Marathon Petroleum, Eaton, Amgen
calendar.why: Pfizer reportedly beat ($0.87 EPS, $16.6B revenue; single source). Shopify options imply ≈±13%, a read on consumer and e-commerce demand into the holidays.
This is the first labor read before Friday's ≈55k payrolls. Openings above ≈7.2M or rising quits keep the 2Y pinned near 4.6% and December ≈75%+. A drop toward 6.9M would help the front end.
Second-tier data that feeds Q4 GDP tracking. It confirms Monday's strong ISM (55.5) or doesn't.

calendar.event: No scheduled Fed speakers; Fed/ECB/NY Fed Global Research Forum opens in Washington (through Nov 4)
calendar.why: Officials may give media interviews on the sidelines. Any comment on whether $100+ oil is a shock to look through moves December odds.
AMD options imply ≈±11% (≈$90B of market cap). It's the next test of the AI-capex trade after Apple's memory-cost warning and Palantir's sell-on-beat.

A sweep raises regulatory risk for tech and AI data centers and changes the fiscal path. Continued GOP control revives deficit and term-premium worries at the long end. Expect overnight moves in 30Y futures and the dollar.

calendar.consensus: Coupon sizes unchanged (dealers); watch 2027 long-end guidance and buyback sizes
calendar.why: This is the main term-premium event of the week. Any hint of smaller long-end auctions in 2027 would extend the bull-flattener. Q4 borrowing was already trimmed to $618B from $628B.

calendar.event: BoE & Norges Bank (Thu); Barkin, Logan (Thu); Oct payrolls ≈55k, Williams, Bowman (Fri)
calendar.why: Payrolls is the last big input before the Dec 8–9 FOMC, where a hike is ≈75% priced.

rates.title: Oil, not the Fed, drove Monday's bull-flattener
rates.body: The 10Y closed ≈4.89–4.91% (intraday low ≈4.865%) and the 30Y ≈5.26–5.29%, down ≈4–5 bp to their lowest since September, while the 2Y held ≈4.56–4.60%. The 10Y is ≈45 bp below its early-October 24-year high of 5.36%. Overnight's Qeshm-driven oil bounce is the first test of whether the move sticks.
rates.simple: A yield is the interest rate a bond pays, and a basis point (bp) is 0.01%. Long-term yields fell because cheaper oil means less inflation down the road, but short-term yields barely moved because traders still expect the Fed to raise rates in December. When long rates fall faster than short ones, the curve 'flattens,' which squeezes banks that borrow short and lend long.

rates.title: Refunding preview: steady coupons, watch 2027 hints
rates.body: Treasury trimmed its Oct–Dec borrowing estimate to $618B from $628B (Newsquawk). Dealers broadly expect unchanged coupon auction sizes at Wednesday's 7:30 AM CT statement. BNP's Dhingra says any change likely comes no earlier than August 2027. The swing factors are guidance on smaller long-end auctions and buyback sizes (Aug baseline: up to $38B liquidity-support, $25B cash-management).
rates.simple: Every quarter Treasury says how much debt it will sell and in what maturities. Selling fewer long-term bonds means less supply for investors to absorb, which tends to lower long-term yields and mortgage rates. Buybacks, where Treasury repurchases older bonds, make the market trade more smoothly.

rates.title: RBA hikes to 4.85% but drops its tightening bias
rates.body: The RBA raised 25 bp to 4.85% in a 6–3 vote (three wanted a hold), its fifth hike of 2026 and the highest cash rate since 2008. The statement removed the 'raise further if needed' language and cited slowing growth, falling house prices and rising unemployment. ActionForex expects a December pause; the next meeting is Dec 8.
rates.simple: Australia's central bank raised its main interest rate again to fight inflation pushed up by energy prices. A split vote and softer wording signal the hiking may be nearly over. When big central banks near a peak, global bond yields usually stop rising so fast.

rates.title: Global yields ease into BoE week; midterms seen as second-order
rates.body: The 10Y gilt was ≈5.20–5.24% (−10 bp Monday), the 10Y Bund ≈3.30–3.32% (lowest since late August) and the 10Y JGB 2.76–2.77% (30Y 3.875%), with BoE and Norges decisions Thursday and a Japanese 10Y auction. Strategists quoted by the Globe and Mail don't expect a change in Congress to materially alter the drivers that pushed U.S. 10s higher this fall. Saxo warns that a fiscal-driven yield rise would weaken, not lift, the dollar.
rates.simple: Government bond rates in the UK, Germany and Japan fell along with U.S. rates as oil dropped. Most strategists think the election matters less for bonds than inflation and Fed policy. A 'term premium' is the extra yield investors demand for tying money up for years; worries about deficits raise it.

derivatives.title: Election-week vol is priced above the month
derivatives.body: Saxo's options brief has the S&P pricing ≈0.86% for today and ≈1.85% into Nov 6 (payrolls). Single-name event vol is elevated: AMD ≈±10.9% (≈$90.7B swing, Benzinga) and Shopify ≈±13%. FedWatch December hike odds are ≈72–77%, down from ≈85–86% in the days after the Oct 28 FOMC.
derivatives.simple: Option prices reveal how big a move traders expect. They see a larger-than-usual move this week because of the election and Friday's jobs report. Implied volatility (the move baked into option prices) tends to drop sharply once a known event passes, which hurts option buyers who wait too long.

derivatives.title: CME's Q3: rates volume and data drive a record quarter
derivatives.body: CME posted record Q3 revenue of $1.74B (+13% y/y) and adjusted EPS of $3.02 vs $2.98 expected. Market-data revenue hit a record ≈$243M (≈14% of revenue). September ADV was a record 31.8M contracts (+22%), with interest-rate ADV 16.2M (+22%) and Treasury futures and options 9.5M (+42%).
derivatives.simple: CME runs the main U.S. futures exchange in Chicago and earns a fee on every contract traded. When investors are unsure where interest rates are headed, they hedge with Treasury and SOFR futures, so volatility in rates is good for CME. Data sales are steadier income that doesn't depend on trading volume.

derivatives.title: Treasury clearing shift starts at BrokerTec
derivatives.body: CME moved BrokerTec U.S. Treasury trades into central clearing from Nov 2 ahead of the SEC's clearing mandate, and plans Treasury-link spreads (cash vs futures) for Q1 2027 pending approval (German-language report, single source). It also listed five Platts dry-freight futures Nov 2.
derivatives.simple: Central clearing puts a clearinghouse between buyer and seller so one firm's default doesn't spread. The SEC is requiring it for much of the Treasury market, which shifts business toward exchanges and clearinghouses such as CME. It also raises collateral costs for some dealers and hedge funds.

metals.title: Gold rejected at $3,970, back to ≈$3,900
metals.body: Spot gold fell ≈1.1% to ≈$3,900–3,905 as the Qeshm oil bounce revived hike fears (Dec ≈75%). Saxo's Ole Hansen flagged renewed selling near $3,970, former support turned resistance, and Saxo calls the picture bearish while below $4,000. Gold is ≈29–30% below January's $5,595 record.
metals.simple: Gold pays no interest, so when markets expect the Fed to raise rates, holding gold looks less attractive than holding bonds. Higher oil prices raise inflation fears and the odds of a rate hike, which hurts gold. Traders watch past price levels where buying or selling previously clustered.

metals.title: WGC: retail is out, central banks are in
metals.body: The World Gold Council halved its 2026 investment-demand growth forecast to 200t from 400t. Q3 bar and coin demand fell 19% to 268t and jewelry 17% to 313t, but central-bank purchases rose 42% to 321t and ETFs took in 211t. The WGC now sees 2026 central-bank buying matching or beating 2025's 848t.
metals.simple: Individuals are buying less gold after a 30% price drop, but central banks keep adding it to reserves to rely less on the dollar. That official buying acts like a floor under the price. ETFs are funds that hold physical gold and trade like stocks.

metals.title: Silver and PGMs lead the drop
metals.body: Silver is ≈$49.8–50.2 (Saxo futures $49.78; one report −3.4%), and SLV traded near 52-week lows pre-market. Platinum fell 2.1% and palladium 2.9%. Silver had bounced ≈3–4% Monday, so this is a round trip.
metals.simple: Silver, platinum and palladium are part precious metal and part industrial input (solar panels, car catalysts), so they swing harder than gold. When rate fears rise and growth looks shaky, they fall twice: as stores of value and as factory inputs.

metals.title: Copper holds near $14,300 on Chilean supply
metals.body: LME 3M copper rose 1.4% Monday to ≈$14,349/t on a softer dollar, cheaper oil and a downgrade to Chile's production outlook, ≈4% under the Sept 9 record of $14,940. LME warehouse stocks rose to 293,775t, the highest since mid-July. Newsquawk had it trading ≈$13,896–14,286 early Tuesday.
metals.simple: Copper is used in wiring, power grids and data centers. Its price rose because the biggest producer, Chile, expects to mine less. But rising warehouse inventories suggest buyers, especially in China, aren't absorbing everything, which caps the price.

banking.title: Anthropic's amended S-1 sets up a mega-IPO for the Street
banking.body: The amended filing shows ≈$17B Q3 revenue (≈+1,127% y/y; +47% q/q vs +144% in Q2), a $567M operating loss and a $23.3B net loss driven by non-cash fair-value charges, plus ≈$895B of compute commitments. Goldman and Morgan Stanley lead a 22-bank syndicate. Valuation talk has slipped to ≈$1.5T from ≈$2T, and the raise could top $100B (unconfirmed).
banking.simple: An S-1 is the disclosure document a company files before selling shares to the public. This would be one of the largest IPOs ever, earning the underwriting banks large fees. The gap between the operating and net loss comes from accounting charges on investor securities, not cash out the door.

banking.title: AI data-center debt is clogging bank balance sheets
banking.body: Banks are delaying the sell-down of a $15B loan for an Anthropic-tied Texas data center after Texas paused new projects over grid risk. JPMorgan, MUFG and others have spent 6+ months distributing $38B of construction debt for Oracle-leased sites. CoreWeave junk yields hit ≈15%, effectively shutting neoclouds out of the high-yield market.
banking.simple: Banks often lend large sums and then sell pieces to investors. When investors won't buy, the loans stay on the bank's books, tying up capital and adding risk. That's a live issue for capital-markets and leveraged-finance desks right now.

banking.title: Fairfax's ≈$5.5B IDBI stake draws protests
banking.body: Canada's Fairfax Financial is buying ≈60.7% of India's IDBI Bank from the government and LIC for ≈528.8B rupees (≈US$5.5–5.6B), pending RBI approval. CNBC reports worker and political opposition.
banking.simple: A Canadian insurer-investor is buying control of a state-linked Indian bank as India sells down its bank stakes. Foreign control of a domestic bank is politically sensitive, which is why unions and politicians are pushing back.

banking.title: Community-bank consolidation keeps closing deals
banking.body: Isabella Bank closed its Grand River Commerce acquisition (Nov 2), Bank7 completed its Century Financial merger (Nov 1) and Laurentian Bank completed its transactions with National Bank and Fairstone (Nov 2). Santander–Webster ($12.2B, announced Feb) remains the largest pending U.S. regional deal. No new sizable U.S. bank deal was announced Monday.
banking.simple: Small banks are merging to spread rising tech and compliance costs across more customers. Deals that close add scale, while bankers say larger regional mergers are waiting on calmer markets and geopolitics.
banking.source: SEC filings; PR Newswire; National Bank

cnbc.title: Apple slides on margin guide in Ternus's first quarter
cnbc.body: Revenue was a record $114.5B (+12%), with 47.9% gross margin (≈1 pt from tariff refunds). December-quarter guidance calls for 7–10% revenue growth but 45–46% gross margin vs ≈46.3% expected, on memory costs Ternus called 'unprecedented.' Shares were ≈−4.5% pre-market.
cnbc.simple: Apple sold more than ever, but the memory chips in its devices are getting much more expensive because AI data centers are buying them up. Gross margin is the share of each sales dollar left after production costs; Apple expects to keep less of each dollar.

cnbc.title: Palantir beats and raises, stock falls anyway
cnbc.body: Q3 revenue was $2.31B (+96%) vs ≈$2.18B expected, adjusted EPS $0.44 vs $0.41, and commercial revenue topped $1B. FY26 guidance rose to ≈$8.53B, with Q4 at ≈$2.65B vs $2.46B consensus. Shares were ≈−4% to −8% after hours and pre-market on slowing contract growth.
cnbc.simple: When a stock is priced for perfection, even strong results can disappoint. Investors focused on slowing new contract signings, which predict future revenue, more than on the quarter's beat.

cnbc.title: Treasury yields mixed as oil tumbles ahead of midterms
cnbc.body: The long end rallied ≈4–5 bp as oil fell ≈7%, while the 2Y hovered ≈4.59% intraday. Treasury's Q4 borrowing estimate came in at $618B vs $628B guided.
cnbc.simple: Cheaper oil eased long-run inflation worries, so long-term bonds rallied. Short-term yields track expected Fed moves and stayed put because a December hike is still likely.

cnbc.title: Gold rises from one-year low on softer oil
cnbc.body: Gold rose ≈2% Monday from Friday's one-year low as oil slumped and traders trimmed hike bets to ≈75%. That bounce is fading Tuesday at ≈$3,900.
cnbc.simple: Lower oil means less inflation and fewer rate hikes, which helps gold. The bounce reversed once oil rose again overnight.

wsj.title: U.S. strikes Iran's Qeshm Island near Hormuz
wsj.body: The WSJ, citing U.S. officials, reported a limited 'defensive' strike on Qeshm Island, part of a series of strikes in recent weeks aimed at protecting Hormuz shipping. Brent rebounded ≈1–2% after Monday's 7.6% drop, and Iran's IRGC claimed it downed U.S. drones.
wsj.simple: Qeshm sits in the Strait of Hormuz, the channel for a large share of the world's oil. Military action there threatens supply just as peace talks were lifting hopes, so oil prices rose again.

wsj.title: Anthropic IPO valuation talk slips to ≈$1.5T
wsj.body: After the tech selloff, prospective IPO investors are coalescing around a ≈$1.5–1.6T valuation, down from ≈$2T a week earlier, per WSJ reporting relayed by trackers. The listing is targeted for the week of Nov 16 per the WSJ; others say Thanksgiving week.
wsj.simple: IPO price talk moves with the market. After AI stocks fell sharply in October, investors want a cheaper entry price. A lower valuation still means a huge deal, and the fees go to the banks running it.

tribune.title: CME's market-data business hits a record
tribune.body: CME's data revenue reached a record ≈$243M last quarter, ≈14% of revenue, which helps cushion the stock if trading slows. Shares are ≈$305–306 (≈$108.5B market cap).
tribune.simple: Chicago's CME sells real-time price data to banks and funds in addition to charging trading fees. Data is a subscription-style business, so it holds up when markets get quiet.

tribune.title: Tribune and NYT sue Brave over AI and paywalls
tribune.body: Tribune Publishing's papers (with the Daily News and Orlando Sentinel) and, separately, the New York Times sued Brave Software in Manhattan federal court on Nov 2. They allege it copied paywalled articles for its AI answers and data licensing and stripped publishers' ads.
tribune.simple: Newspapers say an AI-powered browser is using their paid content without permission and cutting their ad revenue. It's one of several copyright fights over who gets paid when AI tools summarize the news.

tribune.title: CME launches dry-freight futures, moves BrokerTec into clearing
tribune.body: Five Platts dry-bulk freight futures (Western Australia, Brazil and U.S. Gulf to Qingdao) began trading Nov 2. CME also started central clearing of BrokerTec Treasury trades ahead of the SEC mandate.
tribune.simple: Freight futures let miners and shippers lock in the cost of moving iron ore and grain to China. Both moves extend the Chicago exchange into new hedging and clearing business.

tribune.title: Chicago Fed's Goolsbee: what's driving inflation matters
tribune.body: Ahead of Monday's event, Newsquawk summarized Goolsbee as calling September inflation data discouraging. He is less concerned if tariffs or Middle East supply drive it than if AI-demand overheating does. No report of his Monday remarks was found.
tribune.simple: The Chicago Fed president's point is that inflation from temporary supply shocks can fade on its own, but inflation from too much demand needs higher rates. That distinction is what decides a December hike.

nyt.title: Apple's profit up 12%, but AI-driven memory costs bite
nyt.body: The NYT's coverage, as digested, highlighted Apple's ≈12% gains in profit and revenue and its warning that AI-driven memory-chip demand is squeezing margins.
nyt.simple: The AI boom is raising costs for consumer-electronics makers, not just lifting chip stocks. That can mean higher device prices or thinner profits.

nyt.title: Anthropic posts $17B revenue and a $23B loss before IPO
nyt.body: Per the NYT digest, Anthropic's Q3 revenue rose ≈12-fold to $17B while it booked a ≈$23B net loss. Fortune notes q/q growth slowed to ≈47% and costs jumped.
nyt.simple: The company is growing extremely fast but spending heavily on computing power, and accounting charges on investor securities inflate the loss. IPO buyers must decide what that growth is worth.

nyt.title: Midterm Election Day: markets see the vote as an overhang lifting
nyt.body: Morgan Stanley analysts said the vote should remove a market overhang. Prediction pricing has Democrats ≈71% to win the Senate, and the market's other flagged risk is renewed U.S. strikes on Iran after the election.
nyt.simple: Uncertainty itself weighs on markets. Once results are known, investors can price policy, though a power shift in Congress could bring more scrutiny of tech and different spending plans.

talking_points.topic: Rates: the curve is trading oil, not the Fed
talking_points.point: Monday was a textbook bull-flattener: oil −7% took 10s and 30s down ≈4–5 bp, while the 2Y stayed ≈4.6% because December is still ≈75% priced. My read is that the front end is anchored by the hike case until payrolls, and the long end is a function of oil and supply. That makes Wednesday's refunding (any hint of smaller long-end auctions in 2027) the key term-premium event. The trade view is to fade 2s10s flattening if oil re-rallies on Hormuz headlines.

talking_points.topic: Metals: gold's buyer base is changing
talking_points.point: Gold is ≈30% off its $5,595 January peak and stuck under $3,970 resistance, yet the WGC shows central banks buying 321t in Q3 (+42%) while bar and coin demand fell 19%. Price-insensitive official demand is replacing rate-sensitive retail. The bear case runs through real yields and a December hike; the floor is sovereign reserve diversification.

talking_points.topic: Capital markets & banking: AI is both the fee pool and the risk
talking_points.point: The Anthropic IPO (Goldman/MS leading 22 banks, $1.5T valuation talk, possibly $100B+) could be the year's biggest ECM fee event. Meanwhile banks are stuck holding AI data-center loans they can't syndicate: a $15B Texas loan and $38B of Oracle-linked construction debt. For a commercial-banking seat, the question is concentration risk and how leveraged-finance pipelines hold up if the AI trade cracks further.

caveats: WebFetch was blocked this run (CNBC, Yahoo, Saxo and others unreachable), so all figures come from search snippets of early-morning reports, and ranges reflect different snapshot times. Index and Treasury levels are Monday closes; Treasury closes differ by 1–4 bp across sources. The Russell 2000 close conflicts across sources. The WSJ, NYT and Tribune buckets use other outlets' coverage, and the outlet actually used is named on each story. Only two WSJ-attributable stories could be confirmed, and no Tribune-originated Chicago business story was found, so that bucket uses other outlets' Chicago coverage. The Pfizer beat, CME's Treasury-link spread plan and the Democratic-Senate odds are single-source. Times are CT.

updates.label: Midday
updates.headline: Chips beat Apple at midday: Nvidia passes Apple as the most valuable company and the Nasdaq 100 is up ≈0.7%, while the 10Y climbs ≈4 bp to ≈4.95% after the hot JOLTS print, with December hike odds still in the mid-to-high 70s.
points: Rates: the 10Y is ≈4.95–4.96%, up ≈4 bp (Benzinga midday; Equity Insider had 4.958% at 9:26 AM CT). That is a couple of bp above the post-open read. The JOLTS beat (7.52M vs 7.13M; FXStreet confirms the 7.523M print and the Aug revision to 7.19M) is pushing yields up, alongside Brent. I found no clean post-JOLTS 2Y or 30Y quote.

Fed odds: December hike ≈75–77% (FXStreet 75%, Schwab 77%) vs ≈75–76% before the print. That is only a small move: the market is waiting for Friday's payrolls (≈55k) and tonight's midterms before adding more.

Equities: Nasdaq 100 +≈0.7% to ≈28,184. Nvidia ≈$5.01T passes Apple ≈$4.83T as Apple falls ≈4–4.5% on its 45–46% gross-margin guide. AMD +≈5% ahead of tonight's print, Broadcom +≈3%, Micron +≈2.6%. The Dow is still lower on Apple's price weight. Clean S&P/Dow point levels weren't available.

Commodities: Brent ≈$106.6 (+≈1.8%) as the Qeshm strike risk premium holds; that report still rests on unnamed U.S. officials. Gold has pared losses, from ≈$3,898–3,909 early to ≈$3,940 (Kitco, 9:04 AM CT, −$6). Silver ≈$48.8 (−≈3.4%) is lagging, and the gold/silver ratio is ≈80 vs ≈78 Monday.

Thesis check: the morning view that soft labor data would help the front end is wrong for today. September factory orders (consensus ≈+1.1%): still no result found. No new bank M&A today; Monday's TexasBank–Haskell deal and Bank7's Century close (Nov 1, ≈$3.3B combined assets) are the latest.
updates.simple: Investors are selling Treasury bonds after the job-openings report, which pushes their yields (the interest rate the government pays to borrow) higher; the 10-year rate drives mortgage pricing. Higher yields usually hurt stocks, but the market's focus today is on chipmakers ahead of AMD's results, and Nvidia is now worth more than Apple. Gold has recovered most of its early drop because the Iran strike makes investors want safe assets. Silver hasn't recovered as much because it trades partly as an industrial metal.

updates.label: Post-open
updates.headline: September JOLTS came in hot at ≈7.52M openings vs ≈7.10–7.13M expected (August revised up to ≈7.19M), adding to the morning's yield back-up (10Y ≈4.93%) while the Nasdaq opened higher despite Apple.
points: JOLTS (Sept): openings ≈7.52M vs ≈7.10–7.13M consensus, +≈333k m/m; August revised to ≈7.19M from 7.08M. Openings rate ≈4.5%; private ≈6.64M, government ≈0.88M; professional/business services led. Only two non-independent sources so far, so treat the figures as provisional until BLS confirms. Quits — not yet found.

Rates: the 10Y was already ≈4.93% (+2 to +3.5 bp) before the 9 AM CT print, giving back part of Monday's rally as oil rebounded. 2Y ≈4.59%. No clean post-JOLTS quote yet, but a beat this size goes against the morning thesis that weak labor data would help the front end. December hike odds were last ≈75%; expect them to edge up, not down.

Stocks at the open: S&P ≈+0.2% to +0.3%, Nasdaq ≈+0.5% to +0.8%, Dow ≈−0.3% to −0.5%. Chips are lifting the Nasdaq even with Apple ≈−4% on its margin guide. Apple's weight in the price-weighted Dow is what's pulling that index down.
Commodities: Brent ≈$106.7–107.0 (+≈2%, Mon settle $104.77). Gold futures ≈$3,921 (−≈1.2%), spot ≈$3,898. Silver ≈$48.7–49.1 (−≈3.6%), now below $50. Copper and DXY: no fresh quotes found.
Factory orders (Sept, consensus ≈+1.1%) also came out at 9 AM CT, but no result was found yet. Next up: AMD after the close (options imply ≈±11%), then the midterm results tonight.
updates.simple: JOLTS is a government survey that counts how many jobs employers are trying to fill. September showed about 400,000 more openings than forecasters expected, which means the job market is tighter than thought. A tight job market can keep pushing wages and prices up, so the Fed is more likely to raise interest rates in December. That pushes up Treasury yields (the interest the government pays to borrow) and, in turn, rates on mortgages and business loans.
